items.title: The attendee’s guide to the AWS re:Invent 2026 AI/ML track
items.summary: AWS re:Invent 2026 includes more than 140 AI/ML track sessions. This attendee’s guide helps you find the breakouts, chalk talks, workshops, and builders’ sessions that fit your role and goals, spanning AI chips, models and inference, agents, agent trust, and sustainability, so you can build a smarter re:Invent schedule.

items.title: Automating AWS Agent Registry updates with push-based architecture
items.summary: This post shows how to keep the AWS Agent Registry current automatically. Using AWS CloudTrail, Amazon EventBridge, AWS Lambda, and AgentCore Identity, an event-driven pipeline detects MCP server changes and pushes updated tool metadata to the registry with no stored secrets, across single- and multi-account environments.

items.title: How DXC Technology built a multi-model AI substrate on Amazon Bedrock
items.summary: DXC Technology runs mission-critical managed IT services for regulated organizations across 70 countries. Learn how DXC built DCX OASIS, its Human+AI operating model, on a governed multi-model substrate in Amazon Bedrock, separating a resilient model substrate from a trusted harness that orchestrates, governs, and audits AI agents at scale.

items.title: Accelerating generative AI delivery with reusable assets
items.summary: Every generative AI team keeps rebuilding the same components: RAG pipelines, document processors, and agent scaffolding. This post shows how to access a curated catalog of 23 production-ready, open source reusable assets from the AWS Generative AI Innovation Center, with real delivery results from DoorDash, Lyft, and Ricoh.

items.title: Accelerating product development with AI-driven lifecycle management (AI-PDLC) in AWS Quick
items.summary: Learn how to build an AI-driven product development lifecycle (AI-PDLC) with a suite of six AWS Quick agents that take you from scattered customer signals to a validated prototype across Discover, Decide, Design, and Prototype, with human approval at every gate and a specification ready to hand to coding agents like Kiro.

items.title: UAEF: A framework-agnostic system for closed-loop evaluation of AI agents
items.summary: The Universal Agent Evaluation Framework (UAEF) is a framework-agnostic system for evaluating AI agents. UAEF converts each framework’s traces into one canonical format, scores them with 36 built-in metrics across 7 dimensions, and stores results so teams can compare agent versions and catch regressions.

items.title: Introducing usage-based pricing for Amazon SageMaker AI bidirectional streaming
items.summary: AWS Marketplace now supports usage-based metering for Amazon SageMaker bidirectional streaming inference, so model providers can charge for what customers actually consume during a live stream. Deepgram is the launch partner, bringing usage-based speech-to-text and text-to-speech billing to AWS Marketplace.

items.title: Introducing Kimi K3.1 Pro on Amazon Bedrock
items.summary: Kimi K3.1 Pro from Moonshot AI is now available on Amazon Bedrock. Learn how to get started through the OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions, Responses, and Converse APIs, optimize inference with explicit prompt caching, and use the model as a coding assistant in OpenCode.

items.title: Build a daily dependency watcher with LangGraph and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore web search
items.summary: The Web Search API in Amazon Bedrock AgentCore gives agents current, cited web results signed with the AWS credentials they already use. In this post, build a daily dependency watcher as a LangGraph graph that researches package ecosystems in parallel, keeps its rules in code, and checks every finding against its cited sources.

items.title: The agent evaluation playbook: Built-in, DeepEval, and AutoEval on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Evaluations
items.summary: When you deploy an agent, whether it is working is really several questions: did it finish the task, stay on topic, leak data, or skip steps? This post shows how to evaluate agents on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore with built-in, DeepEval, and AutoEval evaluators, and how to match each behavior that matters to the right evaluator at the right level.
